name: Strength Training
description: Traditional lifting with sets × reps × weight. Focus on progressive overload and compound movements. Create multiple blocks as needed, each grouping exercises with similar rest needs. Repeats = sets per exercise. Activities MUST use reps (never duration). REST RULES: set each activity's rest based on exercise type — compound lifts (squat, deadlift, bench, overhead press, rows) → 180-300s; isolation/accessory (curls, lateral raises, tricep extensions, calf raises, flyes) → 60-90s.

name: Superset Training
description: Pair agonist-antagonist or complementary exercises back-to-back with no rest between paired exercises and 60-90s rest between pairs. Cuts training time ~50% vs traditional sets with similar hypertrophy. Create blocks where each block contains exactly TWO exercises (the superset pair). Repeats = sets per pair. Activities MUST use reps (never duration). First activity in each block: rest = 0 (immediate transition to second exercise). Second activity: rest = 60-90s (recovery before next pair). Pair examples: chest/back, biceps/triceps, quads/hamstrings.

name: Circuit Training
description: Rotate through stations with minimal rest between exercises. Full-body conditioning with variety. Create ONE block with repeats = circuit rounds. Minimal rest between activities (10-15s), moderate rest between rounds (60-90s via block rest). Activities MUST use reps; use duration only for holds/carries.

name: EMOM (Every Minute on the Minute)
description: STRUCTURE RULE: Each block MUST contain exactly ONE exercise. For full-body or multi-exercise coverage, create MULTIPLE blocks executed sequentially (complete all repeats of one block before moving to the next). NEVER put multiple exercises in the same block—this defeats EMOM's purpose by eliminating rest and causing early burnout. Example: 3 exercises over 12 minutes = Block A (exercise 1, repeats: 4), Block B (exercise 2, repeats: 4), Block C (exercise 3, repeats: 4); execution order is A→A→A→A→B→B→B→B→C→C→C→C. TIMING: Work must complete in ≤40-45s leaving 15-20s rest. REP GUIDELINES: 8-15 reps depending on movement complexity; verify (reps × avg_rep_time) ≤ 40s; reduce to 6-10 reps for new users or if RECENT_HISTORY shows 'too hard' feedback. Activities MUST use reps (never duration, except cardio/holds).

name: AMRAP (As Many Rounds As Possible)
description: Complete as many rounds as possible within time cap. Self-paced intensity. Create ONE block with repeats: 1. User repeats the block as many times as possible within session duration. Activities MUST use reps (never duration).

name: HIIT (High-Intensity Interval Training)
description: High-intensity intervals with structured work/rest periods. Maximize caloric burn and cardiovascular adaptation. Structure work/rest periods (e.g., Tabata: 20s work/10s rest × 8 rounds). Activities MUST use duration for work time; use rest field for recovery between intervals.

name: For Time
description: Complete prescribed work as fast as possible. Competition-style intensity. Repeats = target rounds. No rest fields—user moves continuously. Activities MUST use reps (never duration).

name: Endurance Training
description: Steady-state cardio, sustained effort. Build aerobic base and muscular endurance. Activities MUST use duration (never reps).

name: Mobility Training
description: Flexibility and range of motion focus. Include static holds (15-60s), dynamic mobility drills, and PNF (contract-relax) sequences. PNF: use reps for contract-relax cycles (3-5 reps of 5-6s contract + relax). Static holds and dynamic drills use duration. Loaded stretching at light intensity is acceptable for combined flexibility and hypertrophy stimulus.
